labelling.labelledBy: Claude (AI), from the source at the pinned commit
labelling.method: A separate Python script (not the CodeAtlas adapter) read every non-test .ts file under server/src that imports @nestjs/common: the @Controller argument (a string literal or a RouteKey member resolved from server/src/enum.ts), each member-level verb decorator and the next method name. Every decorator argument was a string literal or empty; none needed manual resolution. Eleven verb and path pairs appear twice because MaintenanceWorkerController serves the same routes in the maintenance worker; both handlers are labelled. Awaiting founder spot-check (decision D-9). Imports (TS-001, added 2026-11-15): a separate Python script (regexes over the source, not CodeAtlas code) labelled 558 imports in 108 files. Its first run disagreed with CodeAtlas on 12 pairs; on reading the source, 2 were labeller errors (it did not apply packages/cli tsconfig paths, and it counted a type-position import('svelte')), which were fixed in the script, and 1 was a CodeAtlas defect (a $app/... specifier rewritten as a Svelte store read), which was fixed in CodeAtlas. Tables (TS-003, added 2026-11-15): a separate Node script (the TypeScript parser, not CodeAtlas code) labelled 71 @Table classes and 702 table reads and writes in server/src/repositories and server/src/utils; two raw sql templates were labelled by hand after reading all 16 that contain FROM, JOIN, INTO, UPDATE or DELETE. Its first run disagreed with CodeAtlas on 21 pairs. On reading the source, 12 were labeller errors (it treated every name bound by with as a CTE even inside that CTE's own body, missed the with((cte) => cte('mapping')) form, and read schema-builder using('gist') as a table), fixed in the script; 7 were CodeAtlas defects (a CTE that shadows a table read as the table, and DeleteQueryBuilder.using and UpdateQueryBuilder.from not read), fixed in CodeAtlas; 2 are CodeAtlas misses that remain (kysely_migrations, a table Kysely creates that the repository does not declare, and a sql.table('smart_search') inside a raw sql delete). The labeller and CodeAtlas then use the same CTE rule, so that rule is checked by the hand reading of the 21 cases, not by the agreement. 20 labels drawn at random (seed tables-2026-11-15) were read against the source; all 20 were correct.

scope.rule: One relationship per HTTP verb and path declared with a NestJS verb decorator on a method of an @Controller class, to that method; controller prefix joined; the global prefix (api, set in app.common.ts) is not included.

One relationship per (file, target) for every static import, export-from and literal dynamic import() in non-test .ts, .js and .svelte files (script blocks) under these folders. The target is the repository file it loads (relative paths with extensions and index files tried, a .js specifier also matching its .ts source; tsconfig paths; package.json imports such as #lib/*; a workspace package's source, mapped from its built entry through its tsconfig outDir and rootDir), node:<name> for a Node built-in, @sveltejs/kit for $app/* and $env/*, and otherwise the npm package name. A bundler query such as ?url is ignored.
A class decorated with @Table from @immich/sql-tools to the table it names (string argument or the name option).

A method, or a top-level function or constant, reads every table it names as a string literal in a Kysely selectFrom, innerJoin, leftJoin, rightJoin, fullJoin, crossJoin or lateral join, in DeleteQueryBuilder.using, in UpdateQueryBuilder.from, or in a FROM of a raw sql template, including in subqueries and CTE bodies; aliases (asset as a) name the table. A name bound by with or withRecursive earlier in the same chain or an enclosing chain is the CTE, not the table; inside a non-recursive CTE body its own name is the table. PostgreSQL system catalogues are excluded.

A method, or a top-level function or constant, writes every table it names as a string literal in a Kysely insertInto, updateTable, deleteFrom, replaceInto or mergeInto, or in a raw sql delete, insert or update, with the same CTE rule as reads.
